title: Linux_Remaiten_Botnet_Investigation_6d6
description: Investigate and respond to the Linux/Remaiten botnet activity on the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential unauthorized access. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that communicates with an external host? Submit the exact service name.
levels.solution:
Check running services and their network connections. The suspicious service is likely the bot-beacon service.

Run the following command to verify:

systemctl list-units --type=service

The answer is: bot-beacon

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and their network connections.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-units --type=service' to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for a service named 'bot-beacon' in the list of running services.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Traffic Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service generating excessive network traffic? Submit the exact service name.
levels.solution:
Examine systemd timers and services related to network activity. The service generating excessive network traffic is likely the bot-flood service.

Run the following command to verify:

systemctl list-timers

The answer is: bot-flood

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine systemd timers and services related to network activity.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-timers' to list all systemd timers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for a timer associated with the 'bot-flood' service.

levels.title: Determine Service Persistence
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the systemd timer responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service? Submit the exact timer name.
levels.solution:
Investigate systemd timers and their associated services. The systemd timer responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service is likely the bot-beacon.timer.

Run the following command to verify:

systemctl list-timers --all

The answer is: bot-beacon.timer

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd timers and their associated services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-timers --all' to list all systemd timers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for a timer named 'bot-beacon.timer' in the list of systemd timers.
